articles.title: SOG Busts Fake Medical Degree Racket That Sold MBBS, MD Credentials to Around 300
articles.excerpt: Rajasthan's SOG arrested four people, including a Class 11 dropout police say worked as a junior resident at Safdarjung Hospital — a claim the hospital categorically denies.
articles.nri_angle: Families in India and abroad rely on hospital credentials being real; the case shows how to verify a doctor's medical council registration before treatment.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Rajasthan Medical Council registrar files a complaint at Jaipur's Ashok Nagar police station over registrations obtained with forged documents.
Ramkishore Mahawar arrested in Delhi; further arrests follow across states through November.

articles.title: Pakistan's Space Push With China's Help Must Shape India's Planning, Says CDS
articles.excerpt: General N S Raja Subramani told a New Delhi seminar that Chinese ISR, navigation and timing capabilities will be available to Pakistan, and pointed to the SBS-3 surveillance programme as India's answer.
articles.nri_angle: The CDS's planning assumption — a combined China-Pakistan space capability — will shape India's defence procurement and its growing private space sector.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Naidu Says South's Share Won't Shrink Under 50% Lok Sabha Seat Rise
articles.excerpt: Backing the Centre's delimitation plan, the Andhra Pradesh chief minister said South India's seats would rise from 129 to 195 while its 23.76% share of the Lok Sabha stays exactly the same.
articles.image_caption: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, right, with JD(S) leader H. D. Kumaraswamy at their joint press conference in New Delhi. Naidu urged all parties to back the Delimitation Bill and its 50% Lok Sabha seat increase.
articles.nri_angle: Delimitation decides how much weight southern states — the home states of much of the US Indian diaspora — carry in the Lok Sabha for the next generation.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cabinet Clears Delimitation Bill With 50% Seat Rise for Every State, Freeze Till 2051
articles.excerpt: The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared a fresh Constitution Amendment Bill linking women's reservation to delimitation, with a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats for every state and the existing inter-state ratio sealed until 2051. The bill goes before a special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30.
articles.nri_angle: The bill would reshape Lok Sabha representation and activate 33% women's reservation; diaspora readers with family constituencies in India will see boundaries and seat counts change only if the amendment clears both Houses in the November 30 sitting.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Special sitting: Lok Sabha meets (also December 1)
Special sitting: Rajya Sabha meets (also December 3)

articles.title: Election Commission Fixes Website Flaw That Exposed Voter Data, Reuters Finds
articles.excerpt: A call-booking feature on the ECI website leaked voters' personal details and identity-document file paths through predictable form reference numbers. Reuters alerted the commission on October 26; the flaw was fixed within hours on Thursday.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who enrol or update voter details through the ECI portal are among the users whose submitted identity documents passed through the affected feature.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bhopal Scientists Build India's First Indigenous H5N1 Vaccine for Chickens
articles.excerpt: ICAR-NIHSAD's inactivated vaccine targets clade 2.3.2.1a, the strain behind most Indian bird flu outbreaks, and is expected to cost around Rs 1-2 a dose once it is manufactured.
articles.nri_angle: A home-grown, low-cost bird flu vaccine strengthens disease control for India's poultry sector, on which egg and chicken prices and farmer livelihoods depend.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Putin Links Kerala Teen's AI Work to Modi's 'Make in India' at Moscow Conference
articles.excerpt: Russian President Vladimir Putin told 16-year-old Raul John Aju that his AI tools help young people find their own solutions, after the Kochi student argued students should master the basics before leaning on AI.
articles.nri_angle: A Class 12 student from Kochi fielding questions from two heads of state in Moscow is a marker of how far India's young AI builders are travelling.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Women Will Get 33% Reservation, Congress Cannot Stop It, Amit Shah Says
articles.excerpt: Speaking on Constitution Day, the Home Minister blamed the Congress for blocking the amendments needed to operationalise the 2023 women's quota law. The Congress says it backed the law and wants it implemented immediately.
articles.image_caption: Archival photograph: Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Raigad.
articles.nri_angle: The quota, once in force, reserves one-third of Lok Sabha and assembly seats for women; its start date turns on the delimitation bills before Parliament from November 30.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nepal Begins Process to Declare 213 Missing Indians Presumed Dead After August Floods
articles.excerpt: Kathmandu has published the missing list from the August 26 Trishuli-Bhotekoshi flash floods. Families of missing Indians have until December 2 to file objections with the Indian Embassy before declarations of death are issued.
articles.image_caption: Floodwater inundates a town in Nepal, submerging streets and reaching the ground floors of buildings along the river.
articles.nri_angle: Families of the 213 missing Indians have a December 2 deadline to check the official list and contact the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Takes Forward Six Urea Plants Under NIPU-2026 in Push for Self-Reliance
articles.excerpt: Six brownfield projects of 12.7 lakh tonnes each — replacing units up to 60 years old — aim to narrow the gap between India's ~400 LMT urea demand and domestic output.
articles.image_caption: Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw addresses a press conference on Union Cabinet decisions in New Delhi. The decisions included taking forward six brownfield urea projects under the National Investment Policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026.
articles.nri_angle: Expanded domestic urea capacity targets India's fertiliser security and import bill, a cost line that flows through to food prices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Madras Fertilizers' plant in Chennai is over 60 years old and will be replaced.
NFL Nangal's plant is 50-55 years old with a current capacity of 4.73 LMT/year, to be replaced by a 12.7 LMT unit.
Brownfield sites enable faster execution and cost efficiency, saving an estimated ₹225 crore annually.
Domestic urea production rose from 225 LMT in 2014-15 to a record 314.07 LMT in 2023-24.
The investment framework sets a return on equity band of 12-16 percent.

dates.event: IIPL plant at Jagdishpur, Uttar Pradesh, established
Chambal Fertilisers' Gadepan complex in Kota, Rajasthan, operational
KRIBHCO's cooperative project at Shahjahanpur, Uttar Pradesh, commissioned
Matix Fertilizers' plant at Panagarh, West Bengal, commissioned
NIPU-2026 policy notified
Press Information Bureau announced six new brownfield urea plants

articles.title: Supreme Court Orders Separate 'High Fat, High Sugar, High Salt' Warnings on Packaged Foods
articles.excerpt: A bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran directed the FSSAI to mandate a separate pictorial hexagon for each nutrient, judged on total sugars and saturated fat, and to report progress on draft regulations in ten weeks.
articles.image_caption: Packaged snack foods, soft drinks and chocolates sold under international brands.
articles.nri_angle: The labelling regime will apply to packaged foods sold across India, including the snacks and sweets diaspora families buy on visits home and in Indian grocery stores abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

items.text: Separate hexagonal warning for each nutrient (fat, sugar, salt)
Each hexagon must occupy 4% to 5% of the principal display panel
Warnings based on total sugars and saturated fat, not added amounts
FSSAI to reformulate nutrient thresholds, not adopt Dietary Guidelines for India 2024 values

dates.event: Judgment reserved in public interest litigation
Supreme Court directs implementation of front-of-package nutrition labelling
FSSAI to report progress on draft regulations
FSSAI's estimated time to issue and finalise draft regulations
Proposed transition period after regulations are finalised

articles.title: US Would Cap India Tariff at 17% If Trade Deal Is Reached, USTR Says
articles.excerpt: USTR Jamieson Greer said Indian goods would face 25% if no deal is reached. India replied that it has no structural excess capacity in any sector and wants an early deal.
articles.nri_angle: The conditional 17% cap sets the ceiling Indian exporters and US importers of Indian goods will plan around while the trade deal is negotiated.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Super 30 Founder Anand Kumar Receives Special Achievement Award in Japan
articles.excerpt: The Patna educator was honoured by CGC Group chairman Atsuhiro Horiuchi for Super 30's free IIT coaching and his Super Infinity initiative to take mathematics learning across borders.
articles.image_caption: Mathematician Anand Kumar, founder of the Super 30 programme in Patna. Kumar received Japan's Special Achievement Award from CGC Group chairman Atsuhiro Horiuchi for making education accessible to disadvantaged children.
articles.nri_angle: A Patna educator's free-coaching model, long followed by diaspora families, receives international recognition in Japan.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Condemns Houthi Attack on Riyadh Tower, Confirms Two Indians Injured
articles.excerpt: The MEA's November 25 statement called for an immediate cessation of attacks on Saudi civilian and energy infrastructure and said the Indian Embassy in Riyadh is assisting the two injured Indians and their families.
articles.nri_angle: Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate communities in the world; the Indian Embassy in Riyadh is assisting the two injured Indians and is the contact point for their families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Doval in Malé: Indian Ocean Must Connect Nations, Not Divide Them
articles.excerpt: At the 8th Colombo Security Conclave, NSA Ajit Doval called for deeper cooperation on maritime security and drug trafficking, and said India would give the grouping its fullest support.
articles.image_caption: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval addresses the 8th Colombo Security Conclave meeting of national security advisers in Malé, Maldives. Doval called for closer regional security cooperation across the Indian Ocean region.
articles.nri_angle: The Colombo Security Conclave is India's main security forum for the Indian Ocean, the sea lanes linking India with the Gulf and Southeast Asia, where large Indian communities live and work.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Colombo Security Conclave meeting begins
Ajit Doval addresses the meeting

articles.title: Modi and Merz Say India-EU Trade Deal Will Unlock New Opportunities
articles.excerpt: In a phone call marking 75 years of India-Germany ties, the two leaders pointed to the concluded India-EU free trade agreement — expected to be signed in December — as the next driver of trade, investment, defence and technology cooperation.
articles.nri_angle: The India-EU pact's mobility framework covers Indian professionals moving to Europe as transferees and service suppliers, and its tariff cuts target the labour-intensive export sectors that employ millions in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's First Human Metabolic Chamber Opens at CMC Vellore
articles.excerpt: The room-sized calorimeter, built by TIFR and CMC Vellore, tracks how volunteers use energy over 24 hours or more, generating India-specific data on diabetes, obesity and metabolism.
articles.image_caption: The entrance sign of Christian Medical College in Vellore. The college's Human Metabolic Chamber Facility, established jointly with the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, was inaugurated on November 23, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: India-specific metabolic data matters to diaspora families managing diabetes and obesity risk rooted in South Asian physiology.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Celebrating Guru Nanak Jayanti: A Festival of Light and Unity
articles.excerpt: Honoring the birth of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism.
articles.image_caption: A mural painting of Guru Nanak from Gurdwara Baba Atal in Amritsar. Guru Nanak Jayanti, or Gurpurab, marks the birth of Guru Nanak, founder of the Sikh faith.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pennsylvania Measles Deaths Rise to Nine as Cases Reach 1,638
articles.excerpt: An unvaccinated Centre County resident is the state's ninth measles-linked death this year; state departments count at least 13 deaths nationally while the CDC has confirmed six.
articles.nri_angle: Indian families in Pennsylvania and across the US should check MMR records: two doses are more than 97% effective, and exposed readers should call a doctor before visiting a facility.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

rows: 46 counties, as of Nov 23 (state health dept)
CDC has confirmed six; tallies differ by method
data_cards.title: Measles in 2026: The Numbers

articles.title: US Measles Cases Jump by 426 in One Week to 5,838, the Largest Rise in Decades
articles.excerpt: The CDC's latest tally is the first since the Pan American Health Organization declared measles endemic in the United States again, ending an elimination status held since 2000.
articles.image_caption: A baby with measles in the Philippines, in a 2014 CDC Global photograph. Confirmed US measles cases rose by 426 in one week to 5,838 as of November 19, according to the CDC.
articles.nri_angle: With 5,838 confirmed cases across 47 jurisdictions and kindergarten MMR coverage down to 92.4%, US-based Indian families should verify every household member's MMR record, especially before holiday travel.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ICMR Survey Puts Anaemia at 56% of Women, Severe Cases Below 2%
articles.excerpt: SAMPADA, ICMR's venous-blood survey of more than 2 lakh people across 183 districts, finds most anaemia is mild and iron deficiency explains only about half of cases among women and children.
articles.nri_angle: The venous-blood survey resets the anaemia numbers diaspora families cite when elderly parents and children in India are tested, and targets treatment at moderate and severe cases.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Runs More Military Exercises With US Than Any Other Country
articles.excerpt: A US fact sheet on the Major Defense Partnership catalogues a 2026 calendar spanning Yudh Abhyas, Tarang Shakti, Tiger Triumph and Malabar, alongside the Javelin deal and a first Quad joint exercise planned for 2027.
articles.image_caption: US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor (centre) poses with Indian Navy officers, including Rear Admiral Srinivas Maddula, and US personnel aboard the aircraft carrier USS George Washington on November 20, 2026. Gor used the visit to highlight expanding India-US military cooperation, joint exercises and information sharing.
articles.nri_angle: The exercise record underpins the US-India strategic relationship that shapes everything from Indo-Pacific security to defence jobs in both countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Food Regulator to Take Bisleri to Court Over Unsafe Water Sample
articles.excerpt: The FSSAI sanctioned prosecution after one lab found a Bisleri packaged-water sample over bromate limits and a referral lab, on the company's own appeal, detected PAHs and also declared it unsafe.
articles.nri_angle: Bisleri is the bottled-water brand most India travellers and returning NRIs reach for first; a prosecution over an unsafe sample is a consumer-safety story for every visit home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi and Nepal's Balen Shah to Flag Off Ayodhya–Janakpur Express on November 23
articles.excerpt: The weekly direct service links Ayodhya Dham and Janakpur Dham over about 604 km with 10 intermediate stops; inaugural specials run November 23–25, with fares and the full regular timetable still to be published.
articles.image_caption: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah (left) and Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The two leaders are scheduled to jointly flag off the Ayodhya-Janakpur Express on November 23.
articles.nri_angle: A direct Ayodhya–Janakpur train gives diaspora pilgrims a single-train Ramayana-circuit journey between India and Nepal for the first time.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

rows: Weekly — Saturdays from Janakpur Dham, Mondays from Ayodhya Cantt
data_cards.title: Ayodhya–Janakpur Express at a glance

articles.title: Manipur Spurious Liquor Death Toll Rises to 17, About 230 People in Hospital
articles.excerpt: Sixteen of the dead are from Chandel district and one from Kakching. Officials say 1,130 people have been screened, six arrests made and 4,600 litres of illicit liquor seized.
articles.nri_angle: For Manipuri families abroad, the confirmed figures — 17 dead, about 230 admitted, screening locations and hospital names — are the verified update to share instead of circulating rumours.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Dedicates Nitish Setu, New Six-Lane Ganga Bridge in Bihar
articles.excerpt: The 19.7 km Kachhi Dargah–Bidupur crossing links Patna and Vaishali districts and anchors a ₹34,470 crore package of Bihar projects inaugurated on Saturday.
articles.nri_angle: A new Ganga crossing cutting Patna–Vaishali travel to about 20-25 minutes matters to diaspora families traveling to north Bihar.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Crash Probe in Final Stage, Government Tells Supreme Court
articles.excerpt: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta sought two to three weeks to finish the AI171 investigation as the court weighs petitions for an independent probe.
articles.image_caption: The tail section of Air India flight AI171 in the wreckage of the Ahmedabad building the aircraft struck after take-off in June 2025.
articles.nri_angle: AI171 was an Ahmedabad-London flight carrying many diaspora families; its final report is the document relatives in India, the UK and North America have waited 17 months for.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi at IIT Kharagpur's 75th Year: 'Break the Limits, Unlock the Possibilities'
articles.excerpt: At the platinum jubilee of India's first IIT, the Prime Minister interacted with 75 students, unveiled a commemorative coin, and pointed to poverty numbers, chip exports and Skyroot's rocket as proof that 'too late' is a mindset.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the platinum jubilee celebrations of IIT Kharagpur.
articles.nri_angle: IIT Kharagpur's alumni are spread across the diaspora's tech and space industries — Modi's shout-out to Skyroot co-founder Pawan Kumar Chandana, an alumnus, lands directly with them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Court Dispatches Summonses to Doval, Goel in Pannun Case via Delhi Courts
articles.excerpt: The Southern District of New York sent the summonses by FedEx to the Patiala House, Tis Hazari and Dwarka courts under the Hague Convention, after service through India's central authority was attempted and rejected — a route New Delhi says is not lawful.
articles.image_caption: National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, photographed at an event.
articles.nri_angle: The service fight decides whether a US civil suit naming India's NSA and a former R&AW chief can proceed at all — a case diaspora readers have followed since the 2023 murder-for-hire allegations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

dates.event: Pannun filed the civil suit in the Southern District of New York.
India rejected the suit as 'fabricated and malicious'.
US court authorized service through Indian courts.

articles.title: India Crosses 1 Crore HPV Vaccine Doses in Less Than Nine Months
articles.excerpt: The national campaign has reached nearly 87% of its target cohort of 14-year-old girls, with six states reporting full coverage of their identified populations.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families with relatives in India, the free single-dose programme means a 14-year-old daughter or niece can be vaccinated at a government facility with a slot booked on U-WIN.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
